messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in OOMs on serving-pool-us-east-2. 8 OOMs in last 3m, 3 node flaps detected. Sample log: `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`

maria: seeing it. i'm oncall and paged. starting triage — raising to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

raj: I can see repeated allocation failures and `nvml: GPU reset` events on node-23. stack trace snippet: ```
E 0x7fffa... cuCtxSynchronize() -> cudaErrorIllegalAddress
  at /opt/runtime/src/attention_paged.cu:412
```

chris: on it. this looks like paged-attn allocator fragmentation + KV cache slow creep. suspect failure after large long-context batches. any customer-facing errors?

sam: yes, support dashboard shows 2% 5xx from hosted-api for last 10m. top impacted route: /v1/generate for customer acct: acct-ztl-99 (3% of their requests failing). notifying support.

maria: immediate mitigations: 1) route traffic off node-23, 2) enable failover to fallback model-variant (quantized small) for affected capacity tier, 3) bump eviction aggressiveness for KV cache on the cluster. will run commands now.

maria: `kubectl cordon node-23 --kubectl-context=prod-us-east-2`

maria: `kubectl drain node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> draining, stopping runtime pods.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: `hotfix/kv-evict-2025` promoted to canary on pools us-east-2 (2/10 pods). CI: green.

raj: pushed a config change to increase `kv_cache_eviction_threshold` from 0.7 -> 0.55 on the affected pool. patch id: cfg-evict-1755. rolling out to runtime-pool-1.

chris: also toggled `allow_model_fallback=true` for hosted-api route mapping; traffic is slowly shifting to fallback variant. monitoring latency.

maria: node-23 showing `container crash` events during drain, kube restarted pod but crashlooped. we isolated and removed from LB. good to keep it offline until postmortem.

sam: customer-support: notified acct-ztl-99 via incident channel, gave ETA ~10-15m and workaround (use smaller context / retry). they acknowledged.

raj: logs after eviction tweak show reduced allocation pressure. OOM count decreased to 1 in last 5m from 8. cuda errors not reappearing on other nodes.

chris: rolling restart remaining pods in the pool with new allocator flags: `--kv-evict-mode=aggressive --paged-alloc-defrag=true`. doing 5% batch restarts.

maria: handoff for night oncall (alex): summary -> cause suspected: paged-attention allocator fragmentation + KV cache warmup causing slow memory creep leading to OOM and subsequent CUDA resets on node-23. mitigations applied: cordon+drain node-23, enabled model fallback, pushed hotfix `hotfix/kv-evict-2025`, lowered eviction threshold, kicked controlled restarts. customer impacted: acct-ztl-99 ~3% errors for 12m, overall hosted-api 2% 5xx. follow-ups: postmortem, permanent allocator defrag, add KV cache LRU metrics, consider proactive restarts for long-tail nodes.

maria: alex, pinging you in case you pick this up: please monitor resurgence, check node health across us-east-2, verify post-deploy that error rate remains <0.1%. handoff checklist in #oncall-handoffs. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Canary to stable promoted: `hotfix/kv-evict-2025` -> stable (10/10 pods) at ts=1755551500.

raj: confirmed stable. OOMs 0 in last 10m, 5xx back to baseline 0.12%.

maria: opening an incident ticket and postmortem doc: https://redwood.in/incident/1755550000 (will attach logs). assigning owners: chris (runtime fix), raj (allocator telemetry), sam (customer comms).

customer-support: acct-ztl-99 responded: "thanks for the quick fix, pushing update to our client to reduce context lengths for next week".

maria: closing thread for now — leaving node-23 offline for deeper debug. if anything spikes, re-alert. :thumbsup:

alex: (handoff ack) thanks, picking this up. will review postmortem and follow up on the defrag timeline.
